speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with pain during urination and a history of a swollen left ankle; can you tell me if you have noticed any redness or warmth in the knee or ankle, and if these episodes are associated with a fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The clinical presentation of asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting the knee and ankle, combined with urethritis (pain with urination) and risk factors for sexually transmitted infections (inconsistent condom use), is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. Given the duration of symptoms and the specific triad of joint, urinary, and likely ocular/mucocutaneous involvement often seen in this condition, a diagnosis of reactive arthritis is appropriate.
